readings.heading: Ὁ Ἀπόστολος — Philippians 2:5–11
verses: 5. Brothers and sisters: let the same mind be among you that was in Christ Jesus.
6. He shared the very form of God; yet he did not treat being equal with God as something to clutch and hold onto.
7. No — he emptied himself. He took the form of a slave; he was born in the likeness of human beings.
8. And being found in human form, he lowered himself, and became obedient — obedient all the way to death, even death on a cross.
9. That is why God lifted him up to the highest place, and gave him the name that stands above every other name.
10. So that at the name of Jesus every knee will bow — in heaven, and on earth, and under the earth.
11. And every tongue will openly say: Jesus Christ is Lord — to the glory of God the Father.

readings.heading: Τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον — Luke 10:38–42, 11:27–28
verses: 38. Now as they were on their way, he entered a certain village. A woman named Martha welcomed him into her house.
39. She had a sister called Mary, who sat at the Lord's feet and listened to his word.
40. But Martha was distracted by much serving. She came up and said: "Lord, do you not care that my sister has left me to serve alone? Tell her then to help me."
41. But the Lord answered her: "Martha, Martha, you are anxious and troubled about many things,
42. but only one thing is needed. Mary has chosen the good portion, which will not be taken away from her."
27. As he said these things, a woman in the crowd raised her voice and said to him: "Blessed is the womb that bore you, and the breasts that you sucked."
28. But he said: "Blessed rather are those who hear the word of God and keep it."
